title: Arithmetic & Geometric Progression
shortDescription: Spot the pattern first — constant difference means AP, constant ratio means GP — then apply the matching term and sum formulas.
genZNote: AP adds the same thing every time, GP multiplies the same thing every time. Confuse the two and every formula after that is wrong — check the pattern before you touch a formula.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.body: The very first step in any progression question is recognising WHICH kind of sequence you're looking at — subtracting consecutive terms gives a constant in an AP; dividing consecutive terms gives a constant in a GP. Verify this on at least three consecutive terms before applying either formula, since not every sequence is one or the other.

sections.heading: Arithmetic Progression — Formulas
bullets: nth term: aₙ = a + (n−1)d, where a = first term, d = common difference.
Sum of n terms: Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n−1)d], equivalently Sₙ = n/2 × (first term + last term).

sections.heading: Geometric Progression — Formulas
bullets: nth term: aₙ = a·r^(n−1), where r = common ratio (r ≠ 0).
Sum of n terms: Sₙ = a(rⁿ−1)/(r−1) for r ≠ 1. When r = 1, every term is identical and Sₙ = a × n instead — the standard formula divides by zero at r=1.

sections.heading: Worked Example — Standard vs Fast Method

steps.name: Fast sanity-check method
steps.explanation: Sₙ = n/2 × (first term + last term). Last term a₁₀ = 3 + 9×4 = 39. S₁₀ = 10/2 × (3+39) = 5 × 42 = 210.
steps.purpose: Same answer via a second route — useful to double-check under exam pressure without redoing the full formula.

sections.heading: Common Traps
bullets: Assuming every sequence must be an AP or a GP — sequences of squares, cubes, or alternating-rule sequences follow neither; always verify the constant-difference or constant-ratio property first.
Using the GP sum formula a(rⁿ−1)/(r−1) when r = 1 — undefined by division by zero; use Sₙ = a×n instead.

Mixing up d and r — d is subtracted/added (AP), r is multiplied/divided (GP); plugging a ratio into an AP formula or a difference into a GP formula silently gives a wrong answer with no error message.

sections.heading: Exam Strategy
bullets: Check the pattern (subtract vs divide) on the first 3 terms before choosing a formula — this single check prevents the most common progression mistake.
When only the first and last term plus n are given for an AP, Sₙ = n/2 × (first + last) is usually the fastest route — no need to find d first.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: AP has a constant additive difference between terms; GP has a constant multiplicative ratio — identify which before applying the term/sum formula.
keyFacts: AP: aₙ = a + (n−1)d, Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n−1)d] = n/2 × (first + last).
GP: aₙ = a·r^(n−1), Sₙ = a(rⁿ−1)/(r−1) for r≠1; Sₙ = a×n when r=1.
commonConfusion: Not every numeric sequence is an AP or a GP — verify the pattern before assuming.

highYieldFacts: Sₙ = n/2 × (first term + last term) is often faster than the full AP sum formula when both endpoints are known.
GP sum formula breaks at r=1; the sequence becomes constant and Sₙ = a×n instead.
commonTraps: Applying an AP formula to a sequence that is actually a GP (or vice versa) without checking the pattern first.
Forgetting the r=1 special case in GP sum questions.
mustRemember: AP: constant difference. GP: constant ratio.
Verify the pattern on at least 3 consecutive terms before applying any formula.
